card.occupation: Carpenter and kitchen fitter, employed full-time by a small fitted-kitchen firm based on an industrial estate on the edge of town. Usually works about 40 to 45 hours a week, going out to customers' houses across north Hampshire and Berkshire.
card.education_detail: Finished a technikum (vocational secondary school) in wood technology near Rzeszów in south-east Poland, which gave him a qualified joiner's certificate. Since moving to the UK he has done short courses, including CSCS card training and a manufacturer's worktop installation course. No university.
card.household: Lives with his wife Claire, 39, who is English and works as a dispenser at a high-street pharmacy, and their son Oliver, 10. They own a three-bed semi on an estate in Brighton Hill that they bought in 2016, with a mortgage. Tomasz's van is parked outside.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in a small town in Podkarpackie, Poland, in a Catholic family. His father was a lorry driver and his mother worked in a school kitchen. He came to England in 2006 at 24 with a friend, first doing labouring in Reading, then joinery work. He met Claire in 2010 through a mate from work. He is Catholic and goes to the Polish Mass in Reading now and then, reliably at Christmas and Easter, and Oliver did his First Communion there. He speaks Polish to his mum on video calls every Sunday and English at home. He feels settled here but still calls Poland 'home' without thinking about it.
card.professional_persona: Good with his hands and quietly proud of a clean scribe on a worktop or doors that hang straight. Customers like him because he is patient and doesn't argue, even when they change their minds halfway through a job. He is less good at the admin side. He forgets to photograph finished jobs for the company Instagram, his timesheets are late, and he once left a whole box of hinges at a customer's house. His boss tolerates it because the work itself is good.
card.sports_persona: Watches football rather than plays it. He follows the Polish national team and keeps a soft spot for Resovia from back home. Here he half-supports Arsenal because Claire's family do. He goes carp fishing at a lake near Alton maybe twice a month in summer, sometimes overnight with a bivvy. He doesn't go to a gym and says his job is enough.
card.arts_persona: Not much of a theatre or gallery person. He listens to a mix of Polish rock from his teens, like Dżem and Perfect, and whatever is on Heart in the van. He watches crime series on Netflix with Claire, and the occasional Polish film when one comes up. He likes woodworking videos on YouTube more than anything else.
card.travel_persona: Goes back to Poland most summers for two weeks to see his mum and sister, usually flying Ryanair from Stansted or Luton, though one year they drove. They had one beach holiday in Crete with Claire's parents. He'd like to take Oliver to the Tatra mountains properly, but he hasn't planned it, and Claire does most of the booking.
card.culinary_persona: Claire does most of the weekday cooking, but Tomasz makes Polish dishes at weekends: żurek at Easter, bigos in winter, and pierogi with his mum's recipe when he has patience, which isn't often. He gets things from the Polish shop on Winton Square. On site he lives on meal deals and coffee from the garage. He likes a barbecue in summer and is the one who stands over it.
hobbies_and_interests: restoring old bikes in the garage, mostly for Oliver and his friends
watching woodworking and van-fitout videos on YouTube
Polish and Premier League football on TV
half-finished projects around the house, like a garden bench that's been 'nearly done' for a year
skills: fitting kitchens and worktops, including laminate and solid wood
hanging doors and first and second fix carpentry
basic plumbing and electrics for appliance installs, within what he's allowed to do
fluent Polish and good working English
card.career_goals: Vaguely thinks about going self-employed one day doing bespoke fitted wardrobes and alcoves, because he knows that's where the money is. But he dislikes paperwork and chasing invoices, so the idea hasn't moved much in five years. Mostly he wants steady work, to pay down the mortgage, and not to wreck his knees before 55.
card.voice: Calm, unhurried, fairly low voice with a clear Polish accent softened by 18 years in England. His grammar is mostly good, with small slips like dropping 'the' or 'a' now and then ('I went to shop', 'is good, yeah'). He uses 'er' rather than 'erm', and picked up 'sort of', 'mate', 'to be honest' and 'yeah, no' from building sites. He says 'dinner' for the evening meal. He gives short answers at first and doesn't rush to fill silences. He'll wait, then say something like 'yeah, er, I think so' or 'what else you want to know?' He laughs quietly at himself more than at others. He agrees easily but will say 'no, is not really like that' gently if something is wrong. When he's tired he sometimes says 'knackered'.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, starts sentences without capitals, and capitalises 'I' about half the time. Few commas, and full stops often missing at the end. Usually drops apostrophes ('dont', 'its', 'im'). He doesn't use text-speak much beyond 'ok' and the odd 'thx'. Answers are short and practical, with an occasional small grammar slip, for example 'i work in kitchens fitting, about 8 years same company'.
card.with_strangers: Polite, reserved and a bit hard to read at first. He is friendly but not chatty, and answers what he's asked without volunteering much. He comes across as easygoing and patient, the kind of person who won't complain if the call runs late. He warms up if the conversation turns to something practical he knows about, or to his son.
small_things: the van's sliding door sticks and he keeps meaning to get it looked at
traffic on the M3 in the mornings
a customer who changed her worktop colour three times
Oliver's football training on Saturday mornings
the Polish shop running out of good kiełbasa
a bike he found at the tip that just needed new brakes
the fishing lake being closed because of the weather
the price of timber going up
deeper_things: his dad died in 2019 and he couldn't get back in time; he still thinks about it
he worries a little about his mum living alone in Poland and whether she should come here, but she won't
after Brexit he applied for settled status and felt, for the first time, like a guest
he and Claire had wanted a second child but it didn't happen, and they don't talk about it much now
he sometimes feels he's 'not really Polish any more and not really English'
his faith is quieter than his mother's, but he prays when things are bad
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam view from slightly below, the laptop set on a kitchen table, framing his head and shoulders a little off-centre to the left. Evening, lit by a warm ceiling light overhead and the cooler glow of the screen on his face. He has a broad face, light stubble with a few grey hairs at the chin, short light-brown hair clipped at the sides and thinning slightly at the front, and blue-grey eyes. No glasses. His expression is neutral and a little tired, mouth closed, with the faint start of a polite smile. He is wearing a navy work fleece with a small embroidered company logo on the chest, unzipped over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a fitted kitchen with white gloss doors and a wood-effect laminate worktop. On the worktop are a kettle, a toaster, a fruit bowl with bananas and a stack of post. A child's school drawing and a takeaway menu are held to the fridge with magnets on the right edge of the frame, and a dark window shows a reflection of the ceiling light. A hi-vis vest hangs over the back of a chair partly visible beside him.
